quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about your next move.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of the lane puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so they are more likely to see you.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, position yourself to be seen in:

options.text: The vehicle's side mirror.
The vehicle's rearview mirror.
The passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind the vehicle. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, ride in which part of the lane?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view and helps drivers in the next lane see your move.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and do not brake.
Shift your weight to the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and do not brake.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and stay in a straight line. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Slow down and exit the road safely.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Recommended but not required.
Only required for new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a DOT-approved helmet. Helmets are the best protection against head and neck injuries.

questions.question: When riding in a group, your formation should:

options.text: Always be single-file.
Depend on the situation.
Always be staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depend on the situation.
questions.explanation: Usually ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Eye protection is:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Recommended but not required.
Only required for new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires eye protection for all riders on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield offers the best protection.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Look over their shoulder when turning or taking a curve.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when turning or taking a curve.
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of turns or curves. This helps both of you lean correctly.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Need less room to stop than larger vehicles.
Need as much room to stop as larger vehicles.
Can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need as much room to stop as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need as much room to stop as other vehicles. Always keep enough space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the road with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop when you approach an emergency scene.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down in the turn.
Turn by using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Lean in the direction of the turn. Always slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not encouraged because you cannot get used to any part of the lane.
Discouraged because it confuses other drivers.
A good idea when road and traffic conditions change.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good idea when road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger on your motorcycle, tell the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Avoid talking and moving unnecessarily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking and moving unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts and sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: If you refuse to take an alcohol test when an officer asks, your license will be suspended for:

options.text: Three months.
Six months.
12 months.

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 months.
questions.explanation: Tennessee's Implied Consent law means you give permission to be tested for alcohol by driving on state roads. If you refuse an alcohol test, your license will be suspended for 12 months.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, ride in:

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is safest when being passed. Riding near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding far from it may cause the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed through with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in that direction.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is slippery.
The sun is shining.
You believe stopping will be normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop. Slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic all require more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: Changing gears while in a curve:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than changing gears before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause your motorcycle to skid.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Downshift immediately to a lower gear.
Move in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.
Relax and steer straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and steer straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven bridge gratings, simply relax and go straight across at a steady speed. Steering in a zigzag pattern is more dangerous than allowing the weaving.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks at an angle, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight within your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Changing your path angle may move you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it signals the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
Has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it signals the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. Doing so may cause the passing driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Give you an escape route.
Expose you to wind blasts.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expose you to wind blasts.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. Your position should prevent other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: A main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes is:

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve. This can cause your motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may have poor traction.

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
The roadway under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel; lane markings; and steel plates or utility hole covers.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road shows:

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.
